For King Tzidkiyahu of Yehudah had confined him, saying, “How dare you prophesy: ‘Thus said Hashem: I am delivering this city into the hands of the king of Bavel, and he shall capture it.

And King Tzidkiyahu of Yehudah shall not escape from the Kasdim; he shall be delivered into the hands of the king of Bavel, aLit. “and his mouth shall speak with his mouth, and his eyes shall see his eyes.”and he shall speak to him face to face and see him in person.-a
And Tzidkiyahu shall be brought to Bavel, there to remain until I take note of him—declares Hashem. When you wage war against the Kasdim, you shall not be successful.’”
Yirmiyahu said: The word of Hashem came to me:

Chanamel, the son of your uncle Shalum, will come to you and say, “Buy my land in Anatot, bLit. “for yours is the procedure of redemption by purchase.”for you are next in succession to redeem it by purchase.”-b

And just as Hashem had said, my cousin Chanamel came to me in the prison compound and said to me, “Please buy my land in Anatot, in the territory of Binyamin; for the right of succession is yours, and you have the duty of redemption. Buy it.” Then I knew that it was indeed the word of Hashem.
So I bought the land in Anatot from my cousin Chanamel. I weighed out the money to him, seventeen shekels of silver.
I wrote a deed, sealed it, and had it witnessed; and I weighed out the silver on a balance.
I took the deed of purchase, the sealed text and the open one cForce of Heb. uncertain.according to rule and law,-c

and gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriyah son of Machseyah in the presence of my kinsman Chanamel, of the witnesses dWith many mss. and ancient versions; so ancient Near Eastern practice. Other mss. and the editions read “who wrote” (i.e., signed their names).who were named-d in the deed, and all the Yehudim who were sitting in the prison compound.
In their presence I charged Baruch as follows:
Thus said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: “Take these documents, this deed of purchase, the sealed text and the open one, and put them into an earthen jar, so that they may last a long time.”
For thus said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: “Houses, fields, and vineyards shall again be purchased in this land.”
But after I had given the deed to Baruch son of Neriyah, I prayed to Hashem:
“Ah, Lord Elokim! You made heaven and earth with Your great might and outstretched arm. Nothing is too wondrous for You!
You show kindness to the thousandth generation, but visit the guilt of the fathers upon their children after them. O great and mighty God whose name is Hashem of Hosts,
wondrous in purpose and mighty in deed, whose eyes observe all the ways of men, so as to repay every man according to his ways, and with the proper fruit of his deeds!
You displayed signs and marvels in the land of Mitzrayim eLit. “to this day.”with lasting effect,-e and won renown in Yisrael and among mankind to this very day.
You freed Your people Yisrael from the land of Mitzrayim with signs and marvels, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terror.
You gave them this land that You had sworn to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey,

and they came and took possession of it. But they did not listen to You or follow Your Teaching; they did nothing of what You commanded them to do. Therefore you have caused all this misfortune to befall them.

Here are the siegemounds, raised against the city to storm it; and the city, because of sword and famine and pestilence, is at the mercy of the Kasdim who are attacking it. What You threatened has come to pass—as You see.
Yet You, Lord Elokim, said to me: Buy the land for money and call in witnesses—when the city is at the mercy of the Kasdim!”
Then the word of Hashem came to Yirmiyahu:
“Behold I am Hashem, the Elokim of all flesh. Is anything too wondrous for Me?
Assuredly, thus said Hashem: I am delivering this city into the hands of the Kasdim and of King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel, and he shall capture it.

And the Kasdim who have been attacking this city shall come and set this city on fire and burn it down—with the houses on whose roofs they made offerings to Ba'al and poured out libations to other gods, so as to vex Me.
For the people of Yisrael and Yehudah have done nothing but evil in My sight since their youth; the people of Yisrael have done nothing but vex Me by their conduct—declares Hashem.
This city has aroused My anger and My wrath from the day it was built until this day; so that it must be removed from My sight

because of all the wickedness of the people of Yisrael and Yehudah who have so acted as to vex Me—they, their kings, their officials, their priests and prophets, and the men of Yehudah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.
They turned their backs to Me, not their faces; though I have taught them persistently, they do not give heed or accept rebuke.
They placed their abominations in the House which bears My name and defiled it;

and they built the shrines of Ba'al which are in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, where they offered up their sons and daughters to Molech—when I had never commanded, or even thought [of commanding], that they should do such an abominable thing, and so bring guilt on Yehudah.

But now, assuredly, thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael, concerning this city of which you say, “It is being delivered into the hands of the king of Bavel through the sword, through famine, and through pestilence”:
See, I will gather them from all the lands to which I have banished them in My anger and wrath, and in great rage; and I will bring them back to this place and let them dwell secure.
They shall be My people, and I will be their Elokim.
I will give them a single heart and a single nature to revere Me for all time, and it shall be well with them and their children after them.

And I will make an everlasting covenant with them that I will not turn away from them and that I will treat them graciously; and I will put into their hearts reverence for Me, so that they do not turn away from Me.
I will delight in treating them graciously, and I will plant them in this land faithfully, with all My heart and soul.
For thus said Hashem: As I have brought this terrible disaster upon this people, so I am going to bring upon them the vast good fortune which I have promised for them.
And fields shall again be purchased in this land of which you say, “It is a desolation, without man or beast; it is delivered into the hands of the Kasdim.”

Fields shall be purchased, and deeds written and sealed, and witnesses called in the land of Binyamin and in the environs of Yerushalayim, and in the towns of Yehudah; the towns of the hill country, the towns of the Shfelah, and the towns of the Negeb. For I will restore their fortunes—declares Hashem.
The word of Hashem came to Yirmiyahu a second time, while he was still confined in the prison compound, as follows:

Thus said Hashem who is planning it,
Hashem who is shaping it to bring it about,
Whose name is Hashem:

Call to Me, and I will answer you,
And I will tell you wondrous things,
Secrets you have not known.

For thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael, concerning the houses of this city and the palaces of the kings of Yehudah that were torn down aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.for [defense] against the siegemounds and against the sword,

and were filled by those who went to fight the Kasdim,<sup class="endFootnote">-a</sup>—with the corpses of the men whom I struck down in My anger and rage, hiding My face from this city because of all their wickedness:
I am going to bring her relief and healing. I will heal them and reveal to them abundanceaMeaning of Heb. uncertain. of true favor.
And I will restore the fortunes of Yehudah and Yisrael, and I will rebuild them as of old.
And I will purge them of all the sins which they committed against Me, and I will pardon all the sins which they committed against Me, by which they rebelled against Me.

And she shall gain through Me renown, joy, fame, and glory above all the nations on earth, when they hear of all the good fortune I provide for them.bI.e., for Yehudah and Yisrael. They will thrill and quiver because of all the good fortune and all the prosperity that I provide for her.

Thus said Hashem: Again there shall be heard in this place, which you say is ruined, without man or beast—in the towns of Yehudah and the streets of Yerushalayim that are desolate, without man, without inhabitants, without beast—

the sound of mirth and gladness, the voice of bridegroom and bride, the voice of those who cry, “Give thanks to Hashem of Hosts, for Hashem is good, for His kindness is everlasting!” as they bring thanksgiving offerings to the House of Hashem. For I will restore the fortunes of the land as of old—said Hashem.
Thus said Hashem of Hosts: In this ruined place, without man and beast, and in all its towns, there shall again be a pasture for shepherds, where they can rest their flocks.

In the towns of the hill country, in the towns of the Shfelah, and in the towns of the Negeb, in the land of Binyamin and in the environs of Yerushalayim and in the towns of Yehudah, sheep shall pass again under the hands of one who counts them—said Hashem.
See, days are coming—declares Hashem—when I will fulfill the promise that I made concerning the House of Yisrael and the House of Yehudah.
In those days and at that time, I will raise up a true branch of David’s line, and he shall do what is just and right in the land.
In those days Yehudah shall be delivered and Yerushalayim shall dwell secure. And this is what she shall be called: “Hashem is our Vindicator.”
For thus said Hashem: There shall never be an end to men of David’s line who sit upon the throne of the House of Yisrael.
Nor shall there ever be an end to the line of the levitical priests before Me, of those who present burnt offerings and turn the meal offering to smoke and perform sacrifices.
The word of Hashem came to Yirmiyahu:
Thus said Hashem: If you could break My covenant with the day and My covenant with the night, so that day and night should not come at their proper time,
only then could My covenant with My servant David be broken—so that he would not have a descendant reigning upon his throne—or with My ministrants, the levitical priests.
Like the host of heaven which cannot be counted, and the sand of the sea which cannot be measured, so will I multiply the offspring of My servant David, and of the Leviyim who minister to Me.
The word of Hashem came to Yirmiyahu:
You see what this people said: “The two families which Hashem chose have now been rejected by Him.” Thus they despise My people, aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.and regard them as no longer a nation.-a
Thus said Hashem: As surely as I have established My covenant with day and night—the laws of heaven and earth—

so I will never reject the offspring of Yaakov and My servant David; I will never fail to take from his offspring rulers for the descendants of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yaakov. Indeed, I will restore their fortunes and take them back in love.

The word which came to Yirmiyahu from Hashem, when King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel and all his army, and all the kingdoms of the earth and all the peoples under his sway, were waging war against Yerushalayim and all its towns:

Thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael: Go speak to King Tzidkiyahu of Yehudah, and say to him: “Thus said Hashem: I am going to deliver this city into the hands of the king of Bavel, and he will destroy it by fire.

And you will not escape from him; you will be captured and handed over to him. aFor the idiom see note at 32.4.And you will see the king of Bavel face to face and speak to him in person;-a and you will be brought to Bavel.
But hear the word of Hashem, O King Tzidkiyahu of Yehudah! Thus said Hashem concerning you: You will not die by the sword.

You will die a peaceful death; and as incensebLit. “burnings.” was burned for your ancestors, the earlier kings who preceded you, so they will burn incense-b for you, and they will lament for you ‘Ah, lord!’ For I Myself have made the promise—declares Hashem.”
The prophet Yirmiyahu spoke all these words to King Tzidkiyahu of Yehudah in Yerushalayim,

when the army of the king of Bavel was waging war against Yerushalayim and against the remaining towns of Yehudah—against Lachish and Azekah, for they were the only fortified towns of Yehudah that were left.
The word which came to Yirmiyahu from Hashem after King Tzidkiyahu had made a covenant with all the people in Yerushalayim to proclaim a releasecOthers “liberty.” among them—
that everyone should set free his Ivri slaves, both male and female, and that no one should keep his fellow Yehudi enslaved.
Everyone, officials and people, who had entered into the covenant agreed to set their male and female slaves free and not keep them enslaved any longer; they complied and let them go.
But afterward they turned about and brought back the men and women they had set free, and forced them into slavery again.
Then it was that the word of Hashem came to Yirmiyahu from Hashem:
Thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael: I made a covenant with your fathers when I brought them out of the land of Mitzrayim, the house of bondage, saying:

“In the seventh yeardI.e., of servitude. Lit. “After a period of seven years”; cf. Deut. 14.28 and 15.1. each of you must let go any fellow Ivri eOr “who sells himself.”who may be sold-e to you; when he has served you six years, you must set him free.” But your fathers would not obey Me or give ear.
Lately you turned about and did what is proper in My sight, and each of you proclaimed a release to his countrymen; and you made a covenant accordingly before Me in the House which bears My name.
But now you have turned back and have profaned My name; each of you has brought back the men and women whom you had given their freedom, and forced them to be your slaves again.

Assuredly, thus said Hashem: You would not obey Me and proclaim a release, each to his kinsman and countryman. Lo! I proclaim your release—declares Hashem—to the sword, to pestilence, and to famine; and I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.

I will make the men who violated My covenant, who did not fulfill the terms of the covenant which they made before Me, [like] the calf which they cut in two so as to pass between the halves:fCf. Gen. 15.9–10, 17–21.
The officers of Yehudah and Yerushalayim, the officials, the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the halves of the calf
shall be handed over to their enemies, to those who seek to kill them. Their carcasses shall become food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.
I will hand over King Tzidkiyahu of Yehudah and his officers to their enemies, who seek to kill them—to the army of the king of Bavel which has withdrawn from you.

I hereby give the command—declares Hashem—by which I will bring them back against this city. They shall attack it and capture it, and burn it down. I will make the towns of Yehudah a desolation, without inhabitant.
The word which came to Yirmiyahu from Hashem in the days of King Yehoyakim son of Yoshiyahu of Yehudah:
Go to the house of the Rechavim and speak to them, and bring them to the House of Hashem, to one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink.
So I took Ya'azanyahu son of Yirmiyahu son of Chavatzinyah, and his brothers, all his sons, and the whole household of the Rechavim;

and I brought them to the House of Hashem, to the chamber of the sons of Chanan son of Yigdalyahu, the man of Elokim, which is next to the chamber of the officials and above the chamber of Ma'aseyah son of Shalum, the guardian of the threshold.
I set bowls full of wine and cups before the men of the house of the Rechavim, and said to them, “Have some wine.”
They replied, “We will not drink wine, for our ancestor, Yonadav son of Rechav, commanded us: ‘You shall never drink wine, either you or your children.

Nor shall you build houses or sow fieldsaLit. “seed.” or plant vineyards, nor shall you own such things; but you shall live in tents all your days, so that you may live long upon the land where you sojourn.’
And we have obeyed our ancestor Yonadav son of Rechav in all that he commanded us: we never drink wine, neither we nor our wives nor our sons and daughters.
Nor do we build houses to live in, and we do not own vineyards or fields for sowing;
but we live in tents. We have obeyed and done all that our ancestor Yonadav commanded us.
But when King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel invaded the country, we said, ‘Come, let us go into Yerushalayim because of the army of the Kasdim and the army of Aram.’ And so we are living in Yerushalayim.”
Then the word of Hashem came to Yirmiyahu:
Thus said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: Go say to the men of Yehudah and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim: “You can learn a lesson [here] about obeying My commands—declares Hashem.

The commands of Yonadav son of Rechav have been fulfilled: he charged his children not to drink wine, and to this day they have not drunk, in obedience to the charge of their ancestor. But I spoke to you persistently, and you did not listen to Me.

I persistently sent you all My servants, the prophets, to say: ‘Turn back, every one of you, from your wicked ways and mend your deeds; do not follow other gods or serve them. Then you may remain on the land that I gave to you and your fathers.’ But you did not give ear or listen to Me.
The family of Yonadav son of Rechav have indeed fulfilled the charge which their ancestor gave them; but this people has not listened to Me.

Assuredly, thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: I am going to bring upon Yehudah and upon all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim all the disaster with which I have threatened them; for I spoke to them, but they would not listen; I called to them, but they would not respond.”

And to the family of the Rechavim Yirmiyahu said: “Thus said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: Because you have obeyed the charge of your ancestor Yonadav and kept all his commandments, and done all that he enjoined upon you,
assuredly, thus said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: There shall never cease to be a man of the line of Yonadav son of Rechav standing before Me.”
In the fourth year of King Yehoyakim son of Yoshiyahu of Yehudah, this word came to Yirmiyahu from Hashem:
Get a scroll and write upon it all the words that I have spoken to you—concerning Yisrael and Yehudah and all the nations—from the time I first spoke to you in the days of Yoshiyahu to this day.
Perhaps when the House of Yehudah hear of all the disasters I intend to bring upon them, they will turn back from their wicked ways, and I will pardon their iniquity and their sin.
So Yirmiyahu called Baruch son of Neriyah; and Baruch wrote down in the scroll, at Yirmiyahu’s dictation, all the words which Hashem had spoken to him.
Yirmiyahu instructed Baruch, “I am in hiding; I cannot go to the House of Hashem.

But you go and read aloud the words of Hashem from the scroll which you wrote at my dictation, to all the people in the House of Hashem on a fast day; thus you will also be reading them to all the Yehudim who come in from the towns.
Perhaps their entreaty will be accepted by Hashem, if they turn back from their wicked ways. For great is the anger and wrath with which Hashem has threatened this people.”
Baruch son of Neriyah did just as the prophet Yirmiyahu had instructed him, about reading the words of Hashem from the scroll in the House of Hashem.

In the ninth month of the fifth year of King Yehoyakim son of Yoshiyahu of Yehudah, all the people in Yerushalayim and all the people coming from Yehudah proclaimed a fast before Hashem in Yerushalayim.

It was then that Baruch—in the chamber of Gmaryahu son of Shafan the scribe, in the upper court, near the new gateway of the House of Hashem—read the words of Yirmiyahu from the scroll to all the people in the House of Hashem.
Michayhu son of Gmaryahu son of Shafan heard all the words of Hashem [read] from the scroll,

and he went down to the king’s palace, to the chamber of the scribe. There he found all the officials in session: Elishama the scribe, Dlayah son of Shmayah, Elnatan son of Achbor, Gmaryahu son of Shafan, Tzidkiyahu son of Chananyah, and all the other officials.
And Michayhu told them all that he had heard as Baruch read from the scroll in the hearing of the people.

Then all the officials sent Yehudi son of Netanyah son of Shelemyahu son of Kushi to say to Baruch, “Take that scroll from which you read to the people, and come along!” And Baruch took the scroll and came to them.
They said, aChange of vocalization yields “Read it again”; cf. Targum and Septuagint.“Sit down and read it-a to us.” And Baruch read it to them.
When they heard all these words, they turned to each other in fear; and they said to Baruch, “We must report all this to the king.”
And they questioned Baruch further, “Tell us how you wrote down all these words bForce of Heb. uncertain.that he spoke.”-b
He answered them, “He himself recited all those words to me, and I would write them down in the scroll in ink.”
The officials said to Baruch, “Go into hiding, you and Yirmiyahu. Let no man know where you are!”
And they went to the king in the court, after leaving the scroll in the chamber of the scribe Elishama. And they reported all these matters to the king.
The king sent Yehudi to get the scroll and he fetched it from the chamber of the scribe Elishama. Yehudi read it to the king and to all the officials who were in attendance on the king.
Since it was the ninth month, the king was sitting in the winter house, with a fire burning in the brazier before him.

And every time Yehudi read three or four columns, [the king] would cut it up with a scribe’s knife and throw it into the fire in the brazier, until the entire scroll was consumed by the fire in the brazier.
Yet the king and all his courtiers who heard all these words showed no fear and did not tear their garments;
moreover, Elnatan, Dlayah, and Gmaryahu begged the king not to burn the scroll, but he would not listen to them.
The king ordered Yerachme'el, the king’s son, and Srayah son of Azriel, and Shelemyahu son of Avde'el to arrest the scribe Baruch and the prophet Yirmiyahu. But Hashem hid them.
The word of Hashem came to Yirmiyahu after the king had burned the scroll containing the words that Baruch had written at Yirmiyahu’s dictation:
Get yourself another scroll, and write upon it the same words that were in the first scroll that was burned by King Yehoyakim of Yehudah.

And concerning King Yehoyakim of Yehudah you shall say: Thus said Hashem: You burned that scroll, saying, “How dare you write in it that the king of Bavel will come and destroy this land and cause man and beast to cease from it?”

Assuredly, thus said Hashem concerning King Yehoyakim of Yehudah: He shall not have any of his line sitting on the throne of David; and his own corpse shall be left exposed to the heat by day and the cold by night.

And I will punish him and his offspring and his courtiers for their iniquity; I will bring on them and on the inhabitants of Yerushalayim and on all the men of Yehudah all the disasters of which I have warned them—but they would not listen.

So Yirmiyahu got another scroll and gave it to the scribe Baruch son of Neriyah. And at Yirmiyahu’s dictation, he wrote in it the whole text of the scroll that King Yehoyakim of Yehudah had burned; and more of the like was added.
Tzidkiyahu son of Yoshiyahu became king instead of Konyahu son of Yehoyakim, for King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel set him up as king over the land of Yehudah.
Neither he nor his courtiers nor the people of the land gave heed to the words which Hashem spoke through the prophet Yirmiyahu.
Yet King Tzidkiyahu sent Yehuchal son of Shelemyahu and Tzefanyah son of the priest Ma'aseyah to the prophet Yirmiyahu, to say, “Please pray on our behalf to Hashem our Elokim.”
(Yirmiyahu could still go in and out among the people, for they had not yet put him in prison.
The army of Paroh had set out from Mitzrayim; and when the Kasdim who were besieging Yerushalayim heard the report, they raised the siege of Yerushalayim.)
Then the word of Hashem came to the prophet Yirmiyahu:

Thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael: Thus shall you say to the king of Yehudah who sent you to Me to inquire of Me: “The army of Paroh, which set out to help you, will return to its own land, to Mitzrayim.
And the Kasdim will come back and attack this city and they will capture it and destroy it by fire.”
Thus said Hashem: Do not delude yourselves into thinking, “The Kasdim will go away from us.” They will not.
Even if you defeated the whole army of the Kasdim that are fighting against you, and only wounded men were left lying in their tents, they would get up and burn this city down!
When the army of the Kasdim raised the siege of Yerushalayim on account of the army of Paroh,
Yirmiyahu was going to leave Yerushalayim and go to the territory of Binyamin aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.to share in some property there-a among the people.
When he got to the Binyamin Gate, there was a guard officer there named Yiriyay son of Shelemyahu son of Chananyah; and he arrested the prophet Yirmiyahu, saying, “You are defecting to the Kasdim!”
Yirmiyahu answered, “That’s a lie! I’m not defecting to the Kasdim!” But Yiriyay would not listen to him; he arrested Yirmiyahu and brought him to the officials.
The officials were furious with Yirmiyahu; they beat him and put him into prison, in the house of the scribe Yehonatan—for it had been made into a jail.
Thus Yirmiyahu came to the aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.pit and the cells,-a and Yirmiyahu remained there a long time.

Then King Tzidkiyahu sent for him, and the king questioned him secretly in his palace. He asked, “Is there any word from Hashem?” “There is!” Yirmiyahu answered, and he continued, “You will be delivered into the hands of the king of Bavel.”
And Yirmiyahu said to King Tzidkiyahu, “What wrong have I done to you, to your courtiers, and to this people, that you have put me in jail?
And where are those prophets of yours who prophesied to you that the king of Bavel would never move against you and against this land?
Now, please hear me, O lord king, and grant my plea: Don’t send me back to the house of the scribe Yehonatan bLit. “and let me not die there.”to die there.”-b

So King Tzidkiyahu gave instructions to lodge Yirmiyahu in the prison compound and to supply him daily with a loaf of bread from the Bakers’ Street—until all the bread in the city was gone. Yirmiyahu remained in the prison compound.
Shfatyah son of Matan, Gedalyahu son of Pashchur, Yuchal son of Shelemyahu, and Pashchur son of Malkiyah heard what Yirmiyahu was saying to all the people:

“Thus said Hashem: Whoever remains in this city shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence; but whoever surrenders to the Kasdim shall live; aLit. “he shall have his life as booty”; cf. 21.9.he shall at least gain his life-a and shall live.
Thus said Hashem: This city shall be delivered into the hands of the king of Bavel’s army, and he shall capture it.”

Then the officials said to the king, “Let that man be put to death, for he disheartensbLit. “weakens the hands of.” the soldiers, and all the people who are left in this city, by speaking such things to them. That man is not seeking the welfare of this people, but their harm!”
King Tzidkiyahu replied, “He is in your hands; the king cannot oppose you in anything!”

So they took Yirmiyahu and put him down in the pit of Malkiyah, the king’s son, which was in the prison compound; they let Yirmiyahu down by ropes. There was no water in the pit, only mud, and Yirmiyahu sank into the mud.
Eved Melech the Kushi, a eunuch who was in the king’s palace, heard that they had put Yirmiyahu in the pit. The king was then sitting at the Binyamin Gate;
so Eved Melech left the king’s palace, and spoke to the king:
“O lord king, those men have acted wickedly in all they did to the prophet Yirmiyahu; they have put him down in the pit, to die there of hunger.” For there was no more bread in the city.
Then the king instructed Eved Melech the Kushi, “Take with you thirtycOne ms. reads “three.” men from here, and pull the prophet Yirmiyahu up from the pit before he dies.”

So Eved Melech took the men with him, and went to the king’s palace, to dEmendation yields “the wardrobe of.”a place below-d the treasury. There they got worn cloths and rags, which they let down to Yirmiyahu in the pit by ropes.
And Eved Melech the Kushi called to Yirmiyahu, “Put the worn cloths and rags under your armpits, inside the ropes.” Yirmiyahu did so,
and they pulled Yirmiyahu up by the ropes and got him out of the pit. And Yirmiyahu remained in the prison compound.

King Tzidkiyahu sent for the prophet Yirmiyahu, and had him brought to him at the third entrance of the House of Hashem. And the king said to Yirmiyahu, “I want to ask you something; don’t conceal anything from me.”
Yirmiyahu answered the king, “If I tell you, you’ll surely kill me; and if I give you advice, you won’t listen to me.”

Thereupon King Tzidkiyahu secretly promised Yirmiyahu on oath: “As Hashem lives who has eMeaning of Heb. uncertain.given us this life,-e I will not put you to death or leave you in the hands of those men who seek your life.”

Then Yirmiyahu said to Tzidkiyahu, “Thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: If you surrender to the officers of the king of Bavel, your life will be spared and this city will not be burned down. You and your household will live.
But if you do not surrender to the officers of the king of Bavel, this city will be delivered into the hands of the Kasdim, who will burn it down; and you will not escape from them.”
King Tzidkiyahu said to Yirmiyahu, “I am worried about the Yehudim who have defected to the Kasdim; that they [the Kasdim] might hand me over to them to abuse me.”
“They will not hand you over,” Yirmiyahu replied. “Listen to the voice of Hashem, to what I tell you, that it may go well with you and your life be spared.
For this is what Hashem has shown me if you refuse to surrender:

All the women who are left in the palace of the king of Yehudah shall be brought out to the officers of the king of Bavel; and they shall say:
The men who were your friends
Have seduced you and vanquished you.
Now that your feet are sunk in the mire,
They have turned their backs [on you].

They will bring out all your wives and children to the Kasdim, and you yourself will not escape from them. You will be captured by the king of Bavel, and fSo Targum and Septuagint and some mss. Most mss. and the editions read “you will burn down this city by fire.”this city shall be burned down.”-f
Tzidkiyahu said to Yirmiyahu, “Don’t let anyone know about this conversation, gLit. “that you may not die.”or you will die.-g

If the officials should hear that I have spoken with you, and they should come and say to you, ‘Tell us what you said to the king; hide nothing from us, hLit. “that we may not kill you.”or we’ll kill you.-h And what did the king say to you?’
say to them, ‘I was presenting my petition to the king not to send me back to the house of Yehonatan to die there.’”
All the officials did come to Yirmiyahu to question him; and he replied to them just as the king had instructed him. So they stopped questioning him, for the conversation had not been overheard.

Yirmiyahu remained in the prison compound until the day Yerushalayim was captured.
When Yerushalayim was captured…iThis clause would read well before 39.3.
In the ninth year of King Tzidkiyahu of Yehudah, in the tenth month, King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel moved against Yerushalayim with his whole army, and they laid siege to it.
And in the eleventh year of Tzidkiyahu, on the ninth day of the fourth month, the [walls of] the city were breached.

All the officers of the king of Bavel entered, and took up quarters at the middle gate—Nergal Saretzer, Samgar Nevu, Sarsechim the Rav Saris,aTitles of officers. Nergal Saretzer the Rav Mag,-a and all the rest of the officers of the king of Bavel.

When King Tzidkiyahu of Yehudah saw them, he and all the soldiers fled. They left the city at night, by way of the king’s garden, through the gate between the double walls; and he set out toward the Arabah.bHoping to escape across the Yarden.

But the Kasdi troops pursued them, and they overtook Tzidkiyahu in the steppes of Yericho. They captured him and brought him before King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel at Rivlah in the region of Chamat; and he put him on trial.
The king of Bavel had Tzidkiyahu’s children slaughtered at Rivlah before his eyes; the king of Bavel had all the nobles of Yehudah slaughtered.
Then the eyes of Tzidkiyahu were put out and he was chained in bronze fetters, that he might be brought to Bavel.
The Kasdim burned down the king’s palace and the housescTaking Heb. singular as collective, with Kimhi. of the people by fire, and they tore down the walls of Yerushalayim.
The remnant of the people that was left in the city, and the defectors who had gone over to him—the remnant of the people that was left—were exiled by Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards, to Bavel.
But some of the poorest people who owned nothing were left in the land of Yehudah by Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards, and he gave them vineyards and fields at that time.
King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel had given orders to Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards, concerning Yirmiyahu:
“Take him and look after him; do him no harm, but grant whatever he asks of you.”
So Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards, and Nevushazba the Rav Saris, and Nergal Saretzer the Rav Mag, and all the commanders of the king of Bavel sent

and had Yirmiyahu brought from the prison compound. They committed him to the care of Gedalyahu son of Achikam son of Shafan, dMeaning of Heb. uncertain.that he might be left at liberty in a house.-d So he dwelt among the people.
The word of Hashem had come to Yirmiyahu while he was still confined in the prison compound:

Go and say to Eved Melech the Kushi: “Thus said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: I am going to fulfill My words concerning this city—for disaster, not for good—and they shall come true on that day in your presence.
But I will save you on that day—declares Hashem; you shall not be delivered into the hands of the men you dread.
I will rescue you, and you shall not fall by the sword. eSee note at 38.2.You shall escape with your life,-e because you trusted Me—declares Hashem.”

The word that came to Yirmiyahu from Hashem, after Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards, set him free at Ramah, to which he had taken him, chained in fetters, among those from Yerushalayim and Yehudah who were being exiled to Bavel.
The chief of the guards took charge of Yirmiyahu, and he said to him, “Hashem your Elokim threatened this place with this disaster;
and now Hashem has brought it about. He has acted as He threatened, because you sinned against Hashem and did not obey Him. That is why this has happened to you.

Now, I release you this day from the fetters which were on your hands. If you would like to go with me to Bavel, come, and I will look after you. And if you don’t want to come with me to Bavel, you need not. See, the whole land is before you: go wherever seems good and right to you.”—

aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.But [Yirmiyahu] still did not turn back.-a—“Or go to Gedalyahu son of Achikam son of Shafan, whom the king of Bavel has put in charge of the towns of Yehudah, and stay with him among the people, or go wherever you want to go.”

The chief of the guards gave him an allowance of food, and dismissed him.
So Yirmiyahu came to Gedalyahu son of Achikam at Mitzpah, and stayed with him among the people who were left in the land.

The officers of the troops in the open country, and their men with them, heard that the king of Bavel had put Gedalyahu son of Achikam in charge of the region, and that he had put in his charge the men, women, and children—of the poorest in the land—those who had not been exiled to Bavel.

So they with their men came to Gedalyahu at Mitzpah—Yishmael son of Netanyah; Yochanan and Yehonatan the sons of Kareach; Srayah son of Tanchumet; the sons of Eifai the Netofati; and Yezanyah son of the Maachati.

Gedalyahu son of Achikam son of Shafan reassuredbLit. “swore to.” them and their men, saying, “Do not be afraid to serve the Kasdim. Stay in the land and serve the king of Bavel, and it will go well with you.

I am going to stay in Mitzpah to attend upon the Kasdim who will come to us. But you may gather wine and figscLit. “summer fruit.” and oil and put them in your own vessels, and settle in the towns you have occupied.”

Likewise, all the Yehudim who were in Moav, Amon, and Edom, or who were in other lands, heard that the king of Bavel had let a remnant stay in Yehudah, and that he had put Gedalyahu son of Achikam son of Shafan in charge of them.

All these Yehudim returned from all the places to which they had scattered. They came to the land of Yehudah, to Gedalyahu at Mitzpah, and they gathered large quantities of wine and figs.cLit. “summer fruit.”
Yochanan son of Kareach, and all the officers of the troops in the open country, came to Gedalyahu at Mitzpah
and said to him, “Do you know that King Ba'alis of Amon has sent Yishmael son of Netanyah to kill you?” But Gedalyahu son of Achikam would not believe them.

Yochanan son of Kareach also said secretly to Gedalyahu at Mitzpah, “Let me go and strike down Yishmael son of Netanyah before anyone knows about it; otherwise he will kill you, and all the Yehudim who have gathered about you will be dispersed, and the remnant of Yehudah will perish!”
But Gedalyahu son of Achikam answered Yochanan son of Kareach, “Do not do such a thing: what you are saying about Yishmael is not true!”

In the seventh month, Yishmael son of Netanyah son of Elishama, who was of royal descent and one of the king’s commanders, came with ten men to Gedalyahu son of Achikam at Mitzpah; and they ate together there at Mitzpah.

Then Yishmael son of Netanyah and the ten men who were with him arose and struck down Gedalyahu son of Achikam son of Shafan with the sword and killed him, because the king of Bavel had put him in charge of the land.
Yishmael also killed all the Yehudim who were with him—with Gedalyahu in Mitzpah—and the Kasdi soldiers who were stationed there.
The second day after Gedalyahu was killed, when no one yet knew about it,
eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Shomron, their beards shaved, their garments torn, and their bodies gashed, carrying meal offerings and frankincense to present at the House of Hashem.
Yishmael son of Netanyah went out from Mitzpah to meet them, weeping as he walked. As he met them, he said to them, “Come to Gedalyahu son of Achikam.”
When they came inside the town, Yishmael son of Netanyah and the men who were with him slaughtered them [and threw their bodies] into a cistern.

But there were ten men among them who said to Yishmael, “Don’t kill us! We have stores hidden in a field—wheat, barley, oil, and honey.” So he stopped, and did not kill them along with their fellows.—

The cistern into which Yishmael threw all the corpses of the men he had killed aSeptuagint reads “was a large cistern, which…”in the affair of Gedalyahu was the one that-a King Asa had constructed on account of King Basha of Yisrael. That was the one which Yishmael son of Netanyah filled with corpses.—

Yishmael carried off all the rest of the people who were in Mitzpah, including the daughters of the king—all the people left in Mitzpah, over whom Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards, had appointed Gedalyahu son of Achikam. Yishmael son of Netanyah carried them off, and set out to cross over to Bnei Amon.
Yochanan son of Kareach, and all the army officers with him, heard of all the crimes committed by Yishmael son of Netanyah.
They took all their men and went to fight against Yishmael son of Netanyah; and they encountered him by the great pool in Givon.
When all the people held by Yishmael saw Yochanan son of Kareach and all the army officers with him, they were glad;
all the people whom Yishmael had carried off from Mitzpah turned back and went over to Yochanan son of Kareach.
But Yishmael son of Netanyah escaped from Yochanan with eight men, and went to Bnei Amon.

Yochanan son of Kareach and all the army officers with him took all the rest of the people whom bEmendation yields “Yishmael son of Netanyah had carried off.”he had rescued from Yishmael son of Netanyah-b from Mitzpah after he had murdered Gedalyahu son of Achikam—the men, soldiers, women, children, and eunuchs whom [Yochanan] had brought back from Givon.
They set out, and they stopped at GerutcAquila reads “the sheepfolds of.” Kimham, near Beit Lechem, on their way to go to Mitzrayim
because of the Kasdim. For they were afraid of them, because Yishmael son of Netanyah had killed Gedalyahu son of Achikam, whom the king of Bavel had put in charge of the land.
Then all the army officers, with Yochanan son of Kareach, Yezanyah son of Hoshayah, and all the rest of the people, great and small, approached
the prophet Yirmiyahu and said, “Grant our plea, and pray for us to Hashem your Elokim, for all this remnant! For we remain but a few out of many, as you can see.
Let Hashem your Elokim tell us where we should go and what we should do.”
The prophet Yirmiyahu answered them, “Agreed: I will pray to Hashem your Elokim as you request, and I will tell you whatever response Hashem gives for you. I will withhold nothing from you.”
Thereupon they said to Yirmiyahu, “Let Hashem be a true and faithful witness against us! We swear that we will do exactly as Hashem your Elokim instructs us through you—
Whether it is pleasant or unpleasant, we will obey Hashem our Elokim to whom we send you, in order that it may go well with us when we obey Hashem our Elokim.”
After ten days, the word of Hashem came to Yirmiyahu.
He called Yochanan son of Kareach and all the army officers, and the rest of the people, great and small,
and said to them, “Thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael, to whom you sent me to present your supplication before Him:
If you remain in this land, I will build you and not overthrow, I will plant you and not uproot; for I regret the punishment I have brought upon you.
Do not be afraid of the king of Bavel, whom you fear; do not be afraid of him—declares Hashem—for I am with you to save you and to rescue you from his hands.
I will dispose him to be merciful to you: he shall show you mercy and aChange of vocalization yields “let you dwell in.”bring you back to-a your own land.
“But if you say, ‘We will not stay in this land’—thus disobeying Hashem your Elokim—
if you say, ‘No! We will go to the land of Mitzrayim, so that we may not see war or hear the sound of the horn, and so that we may not hunger for bread; there we will stay,’
then hear the word of Hashem, O remnant of Yehudah! Thus said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: If you turn your faces toward Mitzrayim, and you go and sojourn there,
the sword that you fear shall overtake you there, in the land of Mitzrayim, and the famine you worry over shall follow at your heels in Mitzrayim too; and there you shall die.

All the men who turn their faces toward Mitzrayim, in order to sojourn there, shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence. They shall have no surviving remnant of the disaster that I will bring upon them.

For thus said Hashem of Hosts, the God of Yisrael: As My anger and wrath were poured out upon the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, so will My wrath be poured out on you if you go to Mitzrayim. You shall become bI.e., a standard by which men execrate and curse; cf. note at 24.9.an execration of woe, a curse-b and a mockery; and you shall never again see this place.
Hashem has spoken against you, O remnant of Yehudah! Do not go to Mitzrayim! Know well, then—for I warn you this day
that you were deceitful at heart when you sent me to Hashem your Elokim, saying, ‘Pray for us to Hashem our Elokim; and whatever Hashem our Elokim may say, just tell us and we will do it.’
I told you today, and you have not obeyed Hashem your Elokim in respect to all that He sent me to tell you—
know well, then, that you shall die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence in the place where you want to go and sojourn.”
When Yirmiyahu had finished speaking all these words to all the people—all the words of Hashem their Elokim, with which Hashem their Elokim had sent him to them—
Azaryah son of Hoshayah and Yochanan son of Kareach and all the arrogant men said to Yirmiyahu, “You are lying! Hashem our Elokim did not send you to say, ‘Don’t go to Mitzrayim and sojourn there’!
It is Baruch son of Neriyah who is inciting you against us, so that we will be delivered into the hands of the Kasdim to be killed or to be exiled to Bavel!”
So Yochanan son of Kareach and all the army officers and the rest of the people did not obey Hashem’s command to remain in the land of Yehudah.

Instead, Yochanan son of Kareach and all the army officers took the entire remnant of Yehudah—those who had returned from all the countries to which they had been scattered and had sojourned in the land of Yehudah,

men, women, and children; and the daughters of the king and all the people whom Nevuzaradan the chief of the guards had left with Gedalyahu son of Achikam son of Shafan, as well as the prophet Yirmiyahu and Baruch son of Neriyah—

and they went to Mitzrayim. They did not obey Hashem.

They arrived at Tachpanches,
and the word of Hashem came to Yirmiyahu in Tachpanches:
Get yourself large stones, and embed them in mortar in the brick structure at the entrance to Paroh’s palace in Tachpanches, with some Yehudim looking on.

And say to them: “Thus said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: I am sending for My servant King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel, and IaSeptuagint reads “he.” will set his throne over these stones which I have embedded. He will spread out his pavilionbMeaning of Heb. uncertain. over them.

He will come and attack the land of Mitzrayim, delivering
Those destined for the plague, to the plague,
Those destined for captivity, to captivity,
And those destined for the sword, to the sword.

And IaSeptuagint reads “he.” will set fire to the temples of the gods of Mitzrayim; he will burn them down and carry themcI.e., the gods. off. He shall wrap himself up in the land of Mitzrayim, as a shepherd wraps himself up in his garment. And he shall depart from there in safety.
He shall smash the obelisks of the Temple of the Sun which is in the land of Mitzrayim, and he shall burn down the temples of the gods of Mitzrayim.
The word which came to Yirmiyahu for all the Yehudim living in the land of Mitzrayim, living in Migdol, Tachpanches, and Nof, and in the land of Patros:
Thus said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: You have seen all the disaster that I brought on Yerushalayim and on all the towns of Yehudah. They are a ruin today, and no one inhabits them,
on account of the wicked things they did to vex Me, going to make offerings in worship of other gods which they had not known—neither they nor you nor your fathers.
Yet I persistently sent to you all My servants the prophets, to say, “I beg you not to do this abominable thing which I hate.”
But they would not listen or give ear, to turn back from their wickedness and not make offerings to other gods;
so My fierce anger was poured out, and it blazed against the towns of Yehudah and the streets of Yerushalayim. And they became a desolate ruin, as they still are today.

And now, thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: Why are you doing such great harm to yourselves, so that every man and woman, child and infant of yours shall be cut off from the midst of Yehudah, and no remnant shall be left of you?

For you vex me by your deeds, making offering to other gods in the land of Mitzrayim where you have come to sojourn, so that you shall be cut off and become a curseaSee note at 24.9; 42.18. and a mockery among all the nations of earth.

Have you forgotten the wicked acts of your forefathers, of the kings of Yehudah and theirbHeb. “his.” wives, and your own wicked acts and those of your wives, which were committed in the land of Yehudah and in the streets of Yerushalayim?
No one has shown contrition to this day, and no one has shown reverence. YoucHeb. “They.” have not followed the Teaching and the laws that I set before you and before your fathers.
Assuredly, thus said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: I am going to set My face against you for punishment, to cut off all of Yehudah.

I will take the remnant of Yehudah who turned their faces toward the land of Mitzrayim, to go and sojourn there, and they shall be utterly consumed in the land of Mitzrayim. They shall fall by the sword, they shall be consumed by famine; great and small alike shall die by the sword and by famine, and they shall become an execrationaSee note at 24.9; 42.18. and a desolation, a curseaSee note at 24.9; 42.18. and a mockery.
I will punish those who live in the land of Mitzrayim as I punished Yerushalayim, with the sword, with famine, and with pestilence.

Of the remnant of Yehudah who came to sojourn here in the land of Mitzrayim, no survivor or fugitive shall be left to return to the land of Yehudah. Though they all long to return and dwell there, none shall return except [a few] survivors.

Thereupon they answered Yirmiyahu—all the men who knew that their wives made offerings to other gods; all the women present, a large gathering; and all the people who lived in Patros in the land of Mitzrayim:
“We will not listen to you in the matter about which you spoke to us in the name of Hashem.

On the contrary, we will do dLit. “everything that has gone forth from our mouth.”everything that we have vowed-d—to make offerings to the Queen of Heaven and to pour libations to her, as we used to do,eCf. 7.18. we and our fathers, our kings and our officials, in the towns of Yehudah and the streets of Yerushalayim. For then we had plenty to eat, we were well-off, and suffered no misfortune.
But ever since we stopped making offerings to the Queen of Heaven and pouring libations to her, we have lacked everything, and we have been consumed by the sword and by famine.

And when we make offerings to the Queen of Heaven and pour libations to her, is it without our husbands’ approval that we have made cakes fMeaning of Heb. uncertain.in her likeness-f and poured libations to her?”
Yirmiyahu replied to all the people, men and women—all the people who argued with him. He said,

“Indeed, the offerings you presented in the towns of Yehudah and the streets of Yerushalayim—you, your fathers, your kings, your officials, and the people of the land—were remembered by Hashem and brought to mind!

When Hashem could no longer bear your evil practices and the abominations you committed, your land became a desolate ruin and a curse,aSee note at 24.9; 42.18. without inhabitant, as is still the case.

Because you burned incense and sinned against Hashem and did not obey Hashem, and because you did not follow His Teaching, His laws, and His exhortations, therefore this disaster has befallen you, as is still the case.”
Yirmiyahu further said to all the people and to all the women: “Hear the word of Hashem, all Yehudim in the land of Mitzrayim!

Thus said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael: You and your wives have gLit. “spoken with your mouth and fulfilled by your hands.”confirmed by deed what you spoke in words:-g ‘We will fulfill the vows which we made, to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and to pour libations to her.’ So fulfill your vows; perform your vows!

“Yet hear the word of Hashem, all Yehudim who dwell in the land of Mitzrayim! Lo, I swear by My great name—said Hashem—that none of the men of Yehudah in all the land of Mitzrayim shall ever again invoke My name, saying, ‘As the Lord Elokim lives!’
I will be watchful over them to their hurt, not to their benefit; all the men of Yehudah in the land of Mitzrayim shall be consumed by sword and by famine, until they cease to be.

Only the few who survive the sword shall return from the land of Mitzrayim to the land of Yehudah. All the remnant of Yehudah who came to the land of Mitzrayim to sojourn there shall learn whose word will be fulfilled—Mine or theirs!
“And this shall be the sign to you—declares Hashem—that I am going to deal with you in this place, so that you may know that My threats of punishment against you will be fulfilled:

Thus said Hashem: I will deliver Paroh Chofra, king of Mitzrayim, into the hands of his enemies, those who seek his life, just as I delivered King Tzidkiyahu of Yehudah into the hands of King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel, his enemy who sought his life.”

The word which the prophet Yirmiyahu spoke to Baruch son of Neriyah, when he was writing these words in a scroll at Yirmiyahu’s dictation, in the fourth year of King Yehoyakim son of Yoshiyahu of Yehudah:
Thus said Hashem, the Elokim of Yisrael, concerning you, Baruch:
You say, “Woe is me! Hashem has added grief to my pain. I am worn out with groaning, and I have found no rest.”
Thus shall you speak to him: “Thus said Hashem: I am going to overthrow what I have built, and uproot what I have planted—aMeaning of Heb. uncertain.this applies to the whole land.-a

And do you expect great things for yourself? Don’t expect them. For I am going to bring disaster upon all flesh—declares Hashem—but I will bCf. note at 21.9.at least grant you your life-b in all the places where you may go.”
The word of Hashem to the prophet Yirmiyahu concerning the nations.

Concerning Mitzrayim, about the army of Paroh Necho, king of Mitzrayim, which was at the river Perat near Karkemish, and which was defeated by King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel, in the fourth year of King Yehoyakim son of Yoshiyahu of Yehudah.

Get ready buckler and shield,
And move forward to battle!

Harness the horses;
Mount, you horsemen!
Fall in line, helmets on!
Burnish the lances,
Don your armor!

Why do I see them dismayed,
Yielding ground?
Their fighters are crushed,
They flee in haste
And do not turn back—
Terror all around!
—declares Hashem.

aLit. “Let not the swift get away, / Let not the warrior escape.”The swift cannot get away,
The warrior cannot escape.-a
In the north, by the river Perat,
They stagger and fall.

Who is this that rises like the Yeor,
Like streams whose waters surge?

It is Mitzrayim that rises like the Yeor,
Like streams whose waters surge,
That said, “I will rise,
I will cover the earth,
I will wipe out towns
And those who dwell in them.

Advance, O horses,
Dash madly, O chariots!
Let the warriors go forth,
Kush and Put, that grasp the shield,
And the Ludim who grasp and draw the bow!”

But that day shall be for the Lord Elokim of Hosts a day when He exacts retribution from His foes. The sword shall devour; it shall be sated and drunk with their blood. For the Lord Elokim of Hosts is preparing a sacrifice in the northland, by the river Perat.

Go up to Gilad and get balm,
Fair Maiden Mitzrayim.
In vain do you seek many remedies,
There is no healing for you.

Nations have heard your shame;
The earth resounds with your screams.
For warrior stumbles against warrior;
The two fall down together.
The word which Hashem spoke to the prophet Yirmiyahu about the coming of King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel to attack the land of Mitzrayim:

Declare in Mitzrayim, proclaim in Migdol,
Proclaim in Nof and Tachpanches!
Say: Take your posts and stand ready,
For the sword has devoured all around you!

Why are your stalwarts swept away?
They did not stand firm,
For Hashem thrust them down;

He made many stumble,
They fell over one another.

They said:
“Up! let us return to our people,
To the land of our birth,
Because of the deadlybMeaning of Heb. uncertain. sword.”

There they called Paroh king of Mitzrayim:
bMeaning of Heb. uncertain.“Braggart who let the hour go by.”-b

As I live—declares the King,
Whose name is Hashem of Hosts—
bMeaning of Heb. uncertain.As surely as Tavor is among the mountains
And Karmel is by the sea,
So shall this come to pass.-b

Equip yourself for exile,
Fair Mitzrayim, you who dwell secure!
For Nof shall become a waste,
Desolate, without inhabitants.

Mitzrayim is a handsome heifer—
A gadflycOr “butcher”; meaning of Heb. uncertain. from the north dMany mss. read “will come upon her.”is coming, coming!-d

The mercenaries, too, in her midst
Are like stall-fed calves;
They too shall turn tail,
Flee as one, and make no stand.
Their day of disaster is upon them,
The hour of their doom.

bMeaning of Heb. uncertain.She shall rustle away like a snake-b
As they come marching in force;
They shall come against her with axes,
Like hewers of wood.

They shall cut down her forest
—declares Hashem—
Though it cannot be measured;
For they are more numerous than locusts,
And cannot be counted.

Fair Mitzrayim shall be shamed,
Handed over to the people of the north.

Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael, has said: I will inflict punishment on AmoneTutelary deity of the city No (Thebes); cf. Nah. 3.8. of No and on Paroh—on Mitzrayim, her gods, and her kings—on Paroh and all who rely on him.

I will deliver them into the hands of those who seek to kill them, into the hands of King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel and into the hands of his subjects. But afterward she shall be inhabited again as in former days, declares Hashem.

But you,
Have no fear, My servant Yaakov,
Be not dismayed, O Yisrael!
I will deliver you from far away,
Your folk from their land of captivity;
And Yaakov again shall have calm
And quiet, with none to trouble him.

But you, have no fear,
My servant Yaakov
—declares Hashem—
For I am with you.
I will make an end of all the nations
Among which I have banished you,
But I will not make an end of you!
I will not leave you unpunished,
But I will chastise you in measure.
The word of Hashem that came to the prophet Yirmiyahu concerning the Plishtim, before Paroh conquered Azah.

Thus said Hashem:
See, waters are rising from the north,
They shall become a raging torrent,
They shall flood the land and its creatures,
The towns and their inhabitants.
Men shall cry out,
All the inhabitants of the land shall howl,

At the clatter of the stamping hoofs of his stallions,
At the noise of his chariots,
The rumbling of their wheels,
Fathers shall not look to their children
Out of aLit. “weakness of hands.”sheer helplessness-a

Because of the day that is coming
For ravaging all the Plishtim,
For cutting off every last ally
Of Tzor and Tzidon.

The remnant from the island of Kaftor.

BaldnessbShaving the head and gashing the body were expressions of mourning; cf. Deut. 14.1. has come upon Azah,

“O sword of Hashem,

Withdraw into your sheath,
Rest and be still!”

How can itdHeb. “you.” be quiet
When Hashem has given it orders
Against Ashkelon and the seacoast,
Given it assignment there?

Concerning Moav.aA number of parallels to this chapter occur in Isa. 15–16.

Thus said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael:
Alas, that Nevo should be ravaged,
Kiryatayim captured and shamed,
-bThe stronghold-b shamed and dismayed!

Moav’s glory is no more;
In Cheshbon they have plannedcHeb. ḥashebu, play on Cheshbon. evil against her:

Destruction and utter ruin!

A distressing cry of anguish is heard:

fMeaning of Heb. uncertain.And be like Aroer in the desert.-f

Surely, because of your trust

Give fMeaning of Heb. uncertain.wings to Moav,

Moav has been secure from his youth on—

Therefore his fine flavor has remained
And his bouquet is unspoiled.
But days are coming—declares Hashem—when I will send men against him to tip him over; they shall empty his vessels and smash his jars.
And Moav shall be shamed because of Kmosh, as the House of Yisrael were shamed because of Beit El, on whom they relied.

How can you say: We are warriors,
Valiant men for war?

Moav is ravaged,
His towns have been entered,
His choice young men
Have gone down to the slaughter
—declares the King whose name is Hashem of Hosts.

The doom of Moav is coming close,
His downfall is approaching swiftly.

Condole with him, all who live near him,
All you who know him by name!
Say: “Alas, the strong rod is broken,
The lordly staff!”

Descend from glory
And sit in thirst,fMeaning of Heb. uncertain.
O inhabitant of Fair Divon;
For the ravager of Moav has entered your town,
He has destroyed your fortresses.

Stand by the road and look out,
O inhabitant of Aroer.
Ask of him who is fleeing
And of her who is escaping:
Say, “What has happened?”

Moav is shamed and dismayed;
Howl and cry aloud!
Tell at the Arnon
That Moav is ravaged!
Judgment has come upon the tableland—upon Cholon, Yahtzah, and Meifa'at;
upon Divon, Nevo, and Beit Divlatayim;
upon Kiryatayim, Beit Gamul, and Beth-meon;
upon Kriyot and Botzrah—upon all the towns of the land of Moav, far and near.

The might of Moav has been cut down,
His strength is broken
—declares Hashem.

Get him drunk
For he vaunted himself against Hashem.
Moav shall vomit till he is drained,
And he too shall be a laughingstock.

Wasn’t Yisrael a laughingstock to you?
Was he ever caught among thieves,
That you should gI.e., in mockery.shake your head-g
Whenever you speak of him?

Desert the cities
And dwell in the crags,
O inhabitants of Moav!
Be like a dove that nests
In the sides of a pit.

We have heard of Moav’s pride—
Most haughty is he—
Of his arrogance and pride,
His haughtiness and self-exaltation.
I know his insolence—declares Hashem—the wickedness that is in him,hCf. note at Isa. 16.6. the wickedness iHeb. “they have.”he has-i committed.

Therefore I will howl for Moav,
I will cry out for all Moav,
IjHeb. “He.” will moan for the men of Kir Cheres.

With greater weeping than for Yazer
I weep for you, O vine of Sivmah,
Whose tendrils crossed the sea,
Reached to the sea,fMeaning of Heb. uncertain. to Yazer.
A ravager has come down
Upon your fig and grape harvests.

Rejoicing and gladness
Are gone from the farm land,
From the country of Moav;
I have put an end to wine in the presses,
No one treads [the grapes] with shouting—
fMeaning of Heb. uncertain.The shout is a shout no more.-f

There is an outcry from Cheshbon to Elale,
They raise their voices as far as Yahatz,
From Tzoar to Choronayim and Eglath-shelishiah.
The waters of Nimrim
Shall also become desolation.

And I will make an end in Moav
—declares Hashem—
Of those who offer at a shrine
And burn incense to their god.

Therefore,
My heart moans for Moav like a flute;
Like a flute my heart moans
For the men of Kir Cheres—
fMeaning of Heb. uncertain.Therefore,
The gains they have made shall vanish-f—

For every head is bald
And every beard is shorn;
On all hands there are gashes,
And on the loins sackcloth.

On all the roofs of Moav,
And in its squares
There is naught but lamentation;
For I have broken Moav
Like a vessel no one wants
—declares Hashem.

How he is dismayed! Wail!
How Moav has turned his back in shame!
Moav shall be a laughingstock
And a shock to all those near him.

For thus said Hashem:
See, he soars like an eagle
And spreads out his wings against Moav!

Kriyot shall be captured
And the strongholds shall be seized.
In that day, the heart of Moav’s warriors
Shall be like the heart of a woman in travail.

And Moav shall be destroyed as a people,
For he vaunted himself against Hashem.

kSee note at Isa. 24.17.Terror, and pit, and trap-k
Upon you who dwell in Moav!
—declares Hashem.

He who flees from the terror
Shall fall into the pit;
And he who climbs out of the pit
Shall be caught in the trap.
For I will bring upon Moav
The year of their doom
—declares Hashem.

In the shelter of Cheshbon
Fugitives halt exhausted;
For fire went forth from Cheshbon,
Flame from the midstlEmendation yields “house.” of Sichon,
Consuming the brow of Moav,
The pate of the people of Shaon.mOr “tumult.”

Woe to you, O Moav!
The people of Kmosh are undone,
For your sons are carried off into captivity,
Your daughters into exile.

But I will restore the fortunes of Moav in the days to come—declares Hashem.

Thus far is the judgment on Moav.

Concerning Bnei Amon.

Thus said Hashem:
Has Yisrael no sons,
Has he no heir?
Then why has MilkomaThe name of the Amoni deity; vocalized Malkam here and in v. 3. dispossessed Gad,
And why have his people settled in Gad’sbHeb. “his.” towns?

Assuredly, days are coming
—declares Hashem—
When I will sound the alarm of war
Against Rabah of Bnei Amon;
It shall become a desolate mound,
And its villages shall be set on fire.
And Yisrael shall dispossess
Those who dispossessed him
—said Hashem.

Howl, O Cheshbon, for Ai is ravaged!
Cry out, O daughters of Rabah!
Gird on sackcloth, lament,
cMeaning of Heb. uncertain.And run to and fro in the sheepfolds.-c
For Milkom shall go into exile,
Together with his priests and attendants.

dMeaning of Heb. uncertain; for “strength” cf. Akkadian emuqu.Why do you glory in strength,
Your strength is drained,-d
O rebellious daughter,
You who relied on your treasures,
[Who said:] Who dares attack me?

I am bringing terror upon you
—declares the Lord Elokim of Hosts—
From all those around you.
Every one of you shall be driven eLit. “each man straight ahead.”in every direction,-e
And none shall gather in the fugitives.
But afterward I will restore the fortunes of Bnei Amon—declares Hashem.

Concerning Edom.

Thus said Hashem of Hosts:
Is there no more wisdom in Teiman?
Has counsel vanished from the prudent?
Has their wisdom gone stale?

Flee, turn away, sit down low,
O inhabitants of Dedan,
For I am bringing Esav’s doom upon him,
The time when I deal with him.

Would they leave no gleanings?
Even thieves in the night

But it is I who have bared Esav,

His offspring is ravaged,
His kin and his neighbors—
gSome Septuagint mss. read “And there is none to say.”He is no more.-g

“Leave your orphans with me,
I will rear them;
Let your widows rely on me!”
For thus said Hashem: If they who rightly should not drink of the cup must drink it, are you the one to go unpunished? You shall not go unpunished: you will have to drink!
For by Myself I swear—declares Hashem—Botzrah shall become a desolation, a mockery, a ruin, and a curse;hCf. note at 24.9 and 42.18. and all its towns shall be ruins for all time.

I have received tidings from Hashem,
And an envoy is sent out among the nations:
Assemble, and move against her,
And rise up for war!

For I will make you least among nations,
Most despised among men.

cMeaning of Heb. uncertain.Your horrible nature,-c
Your arrogant heart has seduced you,
You who dwell in clefts of the rock,
Who occupy the height of the hill!
Should you nest as high as the eagle,
From there I will pull you down
—declares Hashem.
And Edom shall be a cause of appallment; whoever passes by will be appalled and will hissiCf. note at 18.16. at all its wounds.
It shall be like the overthrow of Sedom and Amorah and their neighbors—said Hashem: no man shall live there, no human shall sojourn there.

It shall be as when a lion comes up out of the jungle of the Yarden against a secure pasture: in a moment jEmendation yields “he can harry them [i.e., the sheep] out of it; and what champion could one place in charge of them?”I can harry him out of it and appoint over it anyone I choose.-j Then who is like Me? Who can summon Me? Who is the shepherd that can stand up against Me?

Hear, then, the plan which Hashem has devised against Edom, and what He has purposed against the inhabitants of Teiman:

Surely the shepherd boys
Shall drag them away;
Surely the pasture shall be
Aghast because of them.

At the sound of their downfall
The earth shall shake;
The sound of screaming
Shall be heard at the Sea of Reeds.

See, like an eagle he flies up,
He soars and spreads his wings against Botzrah;
And the heart of Edom’s warriors in that day
Shall be like the heart of a woman in travail.

Concerning Damesek.

Chamat and Arpad are shamed,
For they have heard bad news.
They shake with anxiety,
LikekSo a few mss. Most mss. and editions read “In.” the sea which cannot rest.

Damesek has grown weak,
She has turned around to flee;
Trembling has seized her,
Pain and anguish have taken hold of her,
Like a woman in childbirth.

lEmendation yields “How has the glorious city been deserted”; so Vulgate.How has the glorious city not been deserted,-l
The citadel of my joy!

Assuredly, her young men shall lie fallen in her squares.
And all her warriors shall be stilled in that day
—declares Hashem of Hosts.

I will set fire to the wall of Damesek,
And it shall consume the fortresses of Ben Hadad.

Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Chatzor, which King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel conquered.

Thus said Hashem:
Arise, march against Kedar,
And ravage Bnei Kedem!

They will take away their tents and their flocks,
Their tent cloths and all their gear;
They shall carry off their camels,
And shall proclaim against them:
Terror all around!

Flee, wander far,
Sit down low, O inhabitants of Chatzor
—says Hashem.
For King Nevuchadretzar of Bavel
Has devised a plan against you
And formed a purpose against you:

Rise up, attack a tranquil nation
That dwells secure
—says Hashem—
That has no barred gates,
That dwells alone.

Their camels shall become booty,
And their abundant flocks a spoil;
And I will scatter to every quarter
Those who have their hair clipped;
And from every direction I will bring
Disaster upon them
—says Hashem.

Chatzor shall become a lair of jackals,
A desolation for all time.
No man shall live there,
No human shall sojourn there.
The word of Hashem that came to the prophet Yirmiyahu concerning Eilam, at the beginning of the reign of King Tzidkiyahu of Yehudah:
Thus said Hashem of Hosts: I am going to break the bow of Eilam, the mainstay of their strength.
And I shall bring four winds against Eilam from the four quarters of heaven, and scatter them to all those winds. There shall not be a nation to which the fugitives from Eilam do not come.

And I will break Eilam before their enemies, before those who seek their lives; and I will bring disaster upon them, My flaming wrath—declares Hashem. And I will dispatch the sword after them until I have consumed them.

And I will set My throne in Eilam,
And wipe out from there king and officials
—says Hashem.
But in the days to come I will restore the fortunes of Eilam—declares Hashem.
The word which Hashem spoke concerning Bavel, the land of the Kasdim, through the prophet Yirmiyahu:

Declare among the nations, and proclaim;
Raise a standard, proclaim;
Hide nothing! Say:
Bavel is captured,
BelaNames of the city god of Bavel. is shamed,
MerodachaNames of the city god of Bavel. is dismayed.

Her fetishes dismayed.

No one shall dwell in it,
Both man and beast shall wander away.
In those days and at that time—declares Hashem—the people of Yisrael together with the people of Yehudah shall come, and they shall weep as they go to seek Hashem their Elokim.

My people were lost sheep: their shepherds led them astray, they drove them out to the mountains, they roamed from mount to hill, they forgot their own resting place.
All who encountered them devoured them; and their foes said, “We shall not be held guilty, because they have sinned against Hashem, the true Pasture, the Hope of their fathers—Hashem.”

Flee from Bavel,
Leave the land of the Kasdim,
And be like he-goats that lead the flock!

For see, I am rousing and leading
An assemblage of great nations against Bavel
From the lands of the north.
They shall draw up their lines against her,
There she shall be captured.

For you rejoiced, you exulted,

So your mother will be utterly shamed,
She who bore you will be disgraced.
Behold the end of the nations—
Wilderness, desert, and steppe!

She shall be utterly desolate.
Whoever passes by Bavel will be appalled

All you who draw the bow;
Shoot at her, don’t spare arrows,
For she has sinned against Hashem.

Raise a shout against her all about!
