Surely the pasture shall be
Aghast because of them.

At the sound of Bavel’s capture
The earth quakes,
And an outcry is heard among the nations.

Thus said Hashem:
See, I am rousing a destructive wind
Against Bavel and the inhabitants of Leb-kamai.aA cipher for Kasdim, “Kasdim.”

I will send strangersbChange of vocalization yields “winnowers.” against Bavel, and they shall winnow her.
And they shall strip her land bare;
They shall beset her on all sides
On the day of disaster.

LetcSome Heb. mss. and ancient versions read “Let not” here and in next line. the archer draw his bow,
And let him stand ready in his coat of mail!
Show no pity to her young men,
Wipe out all her host!

Let them fall slain in the land of Kasdim,
Pierced through in her streets.

For Yisrael and Yehudah were not bereftdLit. “widowed.”
Of their Elokim Hashem of Hosts,
But their land was filled with guilt
Before the Holy One of Yisrael.

Flee from the midst of Bavel
And save your lives, each of you!
Do not perish for her iniquity;
For this is a time of vengeance for Hashem,
He will deal retribution to her.

Bavel was a golden cup in Hashem’s hand,
It made the whole earth drunk;
The nations drank of her wine—
That is why the nations are mad.

Suddenly Bavel has fallen and is shattered;
Howl over her!
Get balm for her wounds:
Perhaps she can be healed.

We tried to cure Bavel
But she was incurable.
Let us leave her and go,
Each to his own land;
For her punishment reaches to heaven,
It is as high as the sky.

Hashem has proclaimed our vindication;
Come, let us recount in Tziyon
The deeds of Hashem our Elokim.

Polish the arrows,
Fill the quivers!
Hashem has roused the spirit of the kings of Madai,
For His plan against Bavel is to destroy her.
This is the vengeance of Hashem,
Vengeance for His Temple.

Raise a standard against the walls of Bavel!
Set up a blockade; station watchmen;
Prepare those in ambush.
For Hashem has both planned and performed
What He decreed against the inhabitants of Bavel.

O you who dwell by great waters,
With vast storehouses,
Your time is come, eMeaning of Heb. uncertain.the hour of your end.-e

Hashem of Hosts has sworn by Himself:
I will fill you with men like a locust swarm,
They will raise a shout against you.

He made the earth by His might,
Established the world by His wisdom,
And by His understanding stretched out the skies.

fLit. “At the sound of His making.”When He makes His voice heard,-f
There is a rumbling of waters in the skies;
He makes vapors rise from the end of the earth,
He makes lightning for the rain,
And brings forth wind from His treasuries.

Every man is proved dull, without knowledge;
Every goldsmith is put to shame because of the idol,
For his molten image is a deceit—
There is no breath in them.

They are delusion, a work of mockery;
In their hour of doom, they shall perish.

Not like these in the Portion of Yaakov,
For it is He who formed all things;
And [Yisrael is] His very own tribe.
Hashem of Hosts is His name.

You are My war club, [My] weapons of battle;
With you I clubbed nations,
With you I destroyed kingdoms;

With you I clubbed horse and rider,
With you I clubbed chariot and driver,

With you I clubbed man and woman,
With you I clubbed graybeard and boy,
With you I clubbed youth and maiden;

With you I clubbed shepherd and flock,
With you I clubbed plowman and team,
With you I clubbed governors and prefects.

But I will requite Bavel and all the inhabitants of Kasdim
For all the wicked things they did to Tziyon before your eyes
—declares Hashem.

See, I will deal with you, O mountain of the destroyer
—declares Hashem—
Destroyer of the whole earth!
I will stretch out My hand against you
And roll you down from the crags,
And make you a burnt-out mountain.

They shall never take from you
A cornerstone or foundation stone;
You shall be a desolation for all time
—declares Hashem.

Raise a standard on earth,
Sound a horn among the nations,
Appoint nations against her,
Assemble kingdoms against her—
Ararat, Mini, and Ashkenaz—
Designate a marshal against her,
Bring up horses like swarmingeMeaning of Heb. uncertain. locusts!

Appoint nations for war against her—
The kings of Madai,
Her governors and all her prefects,
And all the lands they rule!

Then the earth quakes and writhes,
For Hashem’s purpose is fulfilled against Bavel,
To make the land of Bavel
A waste without inhabitant.

The warriors of Bavel stop fighting,
They sit in the strongholds,
Their might is dried up,
They become women.
Her dwellings are set afire,
Her bars are broken.

Runner dashes to meet runner,
Messenger to meet messenger,
To report to the king of Bavel
That his city is captured, from end to end.

The fords are captured,
And the swamp thicketseMeaning of Heb. uncertain. are consumed in fire;
And the fighting men are in panic.

For thus said Hashem of Hosts, the Elokim of Yisrael:
Fair Bavel is like a threshing floor
Ready to be trodden;
In a little while her harvesttime will come.

“Nevuchadretzar king of Bavel
Devoured me and discomfited me;
He swallowed me like a dragon,
He filled his belly with my dainties,
And set me down like an empty dish;
Then he eMeaning of Heb. uncertain.rinsed me out.-e

Let the violence done me and my kindred
Be upon Bavel,”
Says the inhabitant of Tziyon;
“And let my blood be upon the inhabitants of Kasdim,”
Says Yerushalayim.

Assuredly, thus said Hashem:
I am going to uphold your cause
And take vengeance for you;
I will dry up her sea
And make her fountain run dry.

Bavel shall become rubble,
A den for jackals,
An object of horror and hissing,gSee note at 18.16.
Without inhabitant.

Like lions, they roar together,
They growl like lion cubs.

hEmendation yields “With poison [so Syriac] will I set out their drink / And get them drunk till they fall unconscious” (so ancient versions).When they are heated, I will set out their drink
And get them drunk, that they may become hilarious-h
And then sleep an endless sleep,
Never to awake
—declares Hashem.

I will bring them down like lambs for slaughter,
Like rams and he-goats.

How has SheshachiSee note at 25.26. been captured,
The praise of the whole earth been taken!
How has Bavel become
A horror to the nations!

The sea has risen over Bavel,
She is covered by its roaring waves.

Her towns are a desolation,
A land of desert and steppe,
A land no man lives in
And no human passes through.

And I will deal with Bel in Bavel,
And make him disgorge what he has swallowed,
And nations shall no more gaze on him with joy.
Even the wall of Bavel shall fall.

Depart from there, O My people,
Save your lives, each of you,
From the furious anger of Hashem.

Do not be downhearted or afraid
At the rumors heard in the land:
A rumor will come one year,
And another rumor the next year
Of violence in the land,
And of ruler against ruler.

Assuredly, days are coming,
When I will deal with Bavel’s images;
Her whole land shall be shamed,
And all her slain shall fall in her midst.

Heavens and earth and all that is in them
Shall shout over Bavel;
For the ravagers shall come upon her from the north
—declares Hashem.

Yes, Bavel is to fall
[For] the slain of Yisrael,
As the slain of all the earth
Have fallen through Bavel.

You fugitives from the sword,
Go, don’t delay!
Remember Hashem from afar,
And call Yerushalayim to mind.

“We were shamed, we heard taunts;
Humiliation covered our faces,
When aliens entered
The sacred areas of Hashem’s House.”

Assuredly, days are coming
—declares Hashem—
When I will deal with her images,
And throughout her land the dying shall groan.

Though Bavel should climb to the skies,
Though she fortify her strongholds up to heaven,
The ravagers would come against her from Me
—declares Hashem.

Hark! an outcry from Bavel,
Great destruction from the land of the Kasdim.

For Hashem is ravaging Bavel;
He will put an end to her great din,
Whose roar is like waves of mighty waters,
Whose tumultuous noise resounds.

For a ravager is coming upon Bavel,
Her warriors shall be captured, their bows shall be snapped.
For Hashem is a God of requital,
He deals retribution.

I will make her officials and wise men drunk,
Her governors and prefects and warriors;
And they shall sleep an endless sleep,
Never to awaken
—declares the King whose
name is Hashem of Hosts.

Thus said Hashem of Hosts:
Bavel’s broad wall shall be knocked down,
And her high gates set afire.
Peoples shall labor for naught,
And nations have wearied themselves for fire.

The instructions that the prophet Yirmiyahu gave to Srayah son of Neriyah son of Machseyah, when the latter went withjEmendation yields “at the instance of.” King Tzidkiyahu of Yehudah to Bavel, in the fourth year of [Tzidkiyahu’s] reign. Srayah was quartermaster.eMeaning of Heb. uncertain.
Yirmiyahu wrote down in one scroll all the disaster that would come upon Bavel, all these things that are written concerning Bavel.
And Yirmiyahu said to Srayah, “When you get to Bavel, see that you read out all these words.
And say, ‘O Hashem, You Yourself have declared concerning this place that it shall be cut off, without inhabitant, man or beast; that it shall be a desolation for all time.’
And when you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and hurl it into the Perat.

And say, ‘Thus shall Bavel sink and never rise again, because of the disaster that I will bring upon it. And [nations] shall have wearied themselves [for fire].’”kCf. v. 58, last line.

Thus far the words of Yirmiyahu.

aFor this chapter cf. chap. 39 above and 2 Kings 24–25.Tzidkiyahu was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Yerushalayim for eleven years. His mother’s name was Chamutal, daughter of Yirmiyahu of Livnah.
He did what was displeasing to Hashem, just as Yehoyakim had done.

Indeed, Yerushalayim and Yehudah bMeaning of Heb. uncertain.were a cause of anger for Hashem, so that-b He cast them out of His presence.
Tzidkiyahu rebelled against the king of Bavel.

And in the ninth year of hiscI.e., Tzidkiyahu’s. reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, King Nevuchadretzar moved against Yerushalayim with his whole army. They besieged it and built towers against it all around.
The city continued in a state of siege until the eleventh year of King Tzidkiyahu.
By the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine had become acute in the city; there was no food left for the common people.

Then [the wall of] the city was breached. All the soldiers fled; they left the city by night through the gate between the double walls, which is near the king’s garden—the Kasdim were all around the city—and they set out for the Arabah.dSee note at 39.4.
But the Kasdi troops pursued the king, and they overtook Tzidkiyahu in the steppes of Yericho, as his entire force left him and scattered.
They captured the king and brought him before the king of Bavel at Rivlah, in the region of Chamat; and he put him on trial.
The king of Bavel had Tzidkiyahu’s sons slaughtered before his eyes; he also had all the officials of Yehudah slaughtered at Rivlah.
Then the eyes of Tzidkiyahu were put out, and he was chained in bronze fetters. The king of Bavel brought him to Bavel and put him in prison, [where he remained] to the day of his death.

On the tenth day of the fifth month—that was the nineteenth year of King Nevuchadretzar, the king of Bavel—Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards, came eLit. “he stood before.”to represent-e the king of Bavel in Yerushalayim.
He burned the House of Hashem, the king’s palace, and all the houses of Yerushalayim; he burned down the house of bMeaning of Heb. uncertain.every notable person.-b
The entire Kasdi force that was with the chief of the guards tore down all the walls of Yerushalayim on every side.

The remnant of the people left in the city, the defectors who had gone over to the king of Bavel, and what remained of the craftsmenfApparently after the deportation of 2 Kings 24.14; meaning of Heb. uncertain. were taken into exile by Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards. But some of the poorest elements of the population—
some of the poorest in the land—were left by Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards, to be vine-dressers and field hands.
The Kasdim broke up the bronze columns of the House of Hashem, the stands, and the bronze tank that was in the House of Hashem; and they carried all the bronze away to Bavel.
They also took the pails, scrapers, snuffers, sprinkling bowls, ladles, and all the other bronze vessels used in the service.
The chief of the guards took whatever was of gold and whatever was of silver: basins, fire pans, sprinkling bowls, pails, lampstands, ladles, and jars.
The two columns, the one tank and the twelve bronze oxen which supported it, and the stands, which King Shlomo had provided for the House of Hashem—all these objects contained bronze beyond weighing.
As for the columns, each was eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference; it was hollow, and [the metal] was four fingers thick.

It had a bronze capital above it; the height of each capital was five cubits, and there was a meshwork [decorated] with pomegranates about the capital, all made of bronze; and so for the second column, also with pomegranates.
There were ninety-six pomegranates bMeaning of Heb. uncertain.facing outward;-b all the pomegranates around the meshwork amounted to one hundred.
The chief of the guards also took Srayah the chief priest and Tzefanyah, the deputy priest, and the three guardians of the threshold.

And from the city he took a eunuch who was in command of the soldiers; seven royal privy councilors, who were present in the city; the scribe of the army commander, who was in charge of mustering the people of the land; and sixty of the common people who were inside the city.
Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards, took them and brought them to the king of Bavel at Rivlah.

The king of Bavel had them struck down and put to death at Rivlah, in the region of Chamat.

Thus Yehudah was exiled from its land.
This is the number of those whom Nevuchadretzar exiled in the seventh year: 3,023 Yehudim.
In the eighteenth year of Nevuchadretzar, 832 persons [were exiled] from Yerushalayim.
And in the twenty-third year of Nevuchadretzar, Nevuzaradan, the chief of the guards, exiled 745 Yehudim. The total amounted to 4,600 persons.

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of King Yehoyachin of Yehudah, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month, King Evil Merodach of Bavel, in the year he became king, gLit. “raised the head of.”took note of-g King Yehoyachin of Yehudah and released him from prison.
He spoke kindly to him, and gave him a throne above those of other kings who were with him in Bavel.
He removed his prison garments and [Yehoyachin] ate regularly in his presence the rest of his life.
A regular allotment of food was given him by order of the king of Bavel, an allotment for each day, to the day of his death—all the days of his life.
